# Drivetrain and Bearing Periods — EQ6-R Pro RA Axis

**Dimension:** rotation period of every RA drivetrain element at sidereal rate, and which
element (if any) produces a ~134–138 s signal. Sources: [citations.md](../citations.md).

## Stock EQ6-R / EQ6-R Pro geometry

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Worm drive | 180:1 | [1] |
| Belt stage (worm pulley : motor pulley) | 48:12 | [1], [26] ("12/48 of the stock T2.5 belt") |
| Motor | 1.8° stepper, 64 microsteps, no internal gearbox | [1], [2] |
| Overall ratio / resolution | 720; 9,216,000 counts/rev | [1] |
| Belt (user's installed part) | Maedler T2.5, 6 mm, Lw 177.5 mm, 71 teeth — listed as replacement for EQ6-R stock belts | [8]; user confirmed same part |
| Worm-shaft bearings | 608 (8×22×7 mm); EQ6-R Pro kits contain 4 × 608 plus 6 × 6008, one 30206 (listed as 30206M in [7]), one 32208 | [7], [8], [29] |

Verification: 180 × 48/12 = 720; 720 × 200 × 64 = 9,216,000, consistent with [1].

That the EQ6-R's 608s sit on the worm shaft is inferred, not stated: every EQ6-R Pro kit
contains exactly 4 × 608 [7][8], consistent with two per worm on two axes, and the legacy
EQ6 uses "608 bearings" as worm-gear bearings [15]. No fetched source states the EQ6-R
worm-bearing size outright.

**Generation caution.** Legacy EQ6/NEQ6 Pro uses a 47:12 spur-gear stage (3.9167) with an
idler [3]; Rowan belt kits keep the 47:12 ratio [5][6] and "do[] not fit the EQ6 R Pro" [5].
The worm (180:1) and worm period are the same across generations [3][15]; the motor-stage
period differs.

## Rotation periods

Classic periodic error repeats once per worm revolution ("on a EQ6 mount, the rotation cycle is 8 minutes") [40].
Worm period: OzAndrewJ gives 478.7 s for the 180-tooth EQ6 worm [15]; Valente gives
"479.6894" s for the EQ6r Pro [18]; Sim and Galasso give ~480 s [17]. The figure 478.69 s
used below is 86,164.09 s (one sidereal day) ÷ 180 (est.) — consistent with [15].

| # | Element | Arithmetic | Period |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Worm + 48T worm pulley | 86,164.09 / 180 | 478.69 s (est.) |
| 2 | Worm harmonics 2/3/4 | 478.69 / n | 239.3 / 159.6 / 119.7 s (est.) |
| 3 | 12T motor pulley (EQ6-R) | 478.69 × 12/48 | **119.67 s** (est.) |
| 4 | Belt tooth mesh | 478.69 / 48 | 9.97 s (est.) |
| 5 | Belt revolution, 71T belt | 478.69 × 71/48 | 708.1 s (est.) |
| 6 | Belt 5th harmonic | 708.1 / 5 | 141.6 s (est.) |
| 7 | Motor–belt beat | 1 / (1/119.67 − 1/708.1) | 144.0 s (est.) |
| 8 | Legacy EQ6 motor gear (47:12) | 478.7 × 12/47 | 122.2 s [15][36] |
| 9 | Legacy EQ6 transfer gear | — | 366 s [36] |

Published practitioner mappings agree with rows 3–4: "a 120 s period would indicate the
timing pulley on the RA motor. A 10 s period indicates a loose RA belt" [22]; "The 120 s peak
… is one full revolution of the motor pulley" [26]; a "very precise period of 10 seconds" on
the stock T2.5 belt disappeared after a GT2 15/60 pulley change [26].

### No stock gear element produces 134–138 s

Because the motor turns exactly 4× per worm turn [1], every worm/motor frequency, harmonic,
and sum/difference beat is an integer multiple of the worm frequency, giving periods of
478.69/n only (est.). 134–138 s is 3.47–3.57 worm orders (478.69/138 = 3.469; 478.69/134 =
3.572) — between n = 3 (159.6 s) and n = 4 (119.7 s), not on either. The motor pulley at
119.67 s is 11–15% shorter than the observed band. The belt (rows 5–7) misses at 141.6 s and
144.0 s.

## Worm-shaft bearing (608) defect periods

608 geometry: Z = 7 balls, Dw = 3.969 mm, pitch circle dm = 14.700 mm [9]; "~15.0 mm" [10].
Formulas (inner ring rotating with the worm, outer stationary, cos φ = 1) [11][12]. A ball
defect strikes the races twice per spin, so the observed line is 2 × BSF [11]. Slip "shifts
the actual frequencies one to two percent below the kinematic prediction" [11] — i.e. the
**period lengthens** by 1–2%.

Ratio Bd/Pd: 3.969/14.7 = 0.2700; 3.969/15.0 = 0.2646.

Worked example (dm = 15.0): BSF order = (15.0 / (2 × 3.969)) × (1 − 0.2646²) = 1.8897 × 0.9300 =
1.7573; 2 × BSF = 3.5147; period = 478.69 / 3.5147 = 136.2 s (est.).

| Line | Order (dm 14.7 / 15.0) | Period, dm 14.7: 0% / 1% / 2% slip | Period, dm 15.0: 0% / 1% / 2% slip |
|---|---|---|---|
| FTF (cage) | 0.3650 / 0.3677 | 1311.5 / 1324.7 / 1338.2 s | 1301.8 / 1315.0 / 1328.4 s |
| BPFO (outer race) | 2.5550 / 2.5739 | 187.4 / 189.2 / 191.2 s | 186.0 / 187.9 / 189.8 s |
| BPFI (inner race) | 4.4450 / 4.4261 | 107.7 / 108.8 / 109.9 s | 108.2 / 109.2 / 110.4 s |
| BSF | 1.7169 / 1.7573 | 278.8 / 281.6 / 284.5 s | 272.4 / 275.1 / 278.0 s |
| **2 × BSF (ball defect)** | 3.4337 / 3.5147 | **139.4 / 140.8 / 142.3 s** | **136.2 / 137.6 / 139.0 s** |

All values (est.), computed from [9]–[11] and the 478.69 s worm period.

Observations:

1. **2 × BSF of a standard 608 on the worm shaft is the only element found within reach of
   134–138 s** (136.2–142.3 s (est.)). It overlaps the observed band only at its low end
   (dm 15.0 mm, 0–1% slip). This is a numerical coincidence check, not proof of cause.
2. **BPFI ≈ 107.7–110.4 s (est.)** sits beside the 109.2 s fundamental John Sim inferred for an
   unresolved EQ6R Pro case [17], and Pinguru independently estimated a worm-bearing
   brinelling order of "4,4 times/rotation" [26] (BPFI order 4.43–4.45 here). Not confirmed
   in either thread.
3. Bearing lines are non-integer orders of shaft speed by construction [11], which matches
   the fact that 136 s is not a worm harmonic.
4. **Non-standard 608s change the numbers.** A 4-ball hybrid ceramic "608" exists [14]; the
   Deep Space Products ceramic hybrid worm-bearing kit publishes no ball count or diameter
   [13]. FTF and BSF depend only on Bd/Pd, not on ball count; BPFO/BPFI scale with Z.
   Without the installed bearing's geometry, its exact lines cannot be computed.

## Gaps and limitations

- Sky-Watcher publishes no belt tooth count, worm-bearing size, or worm start count [1]. The
  71T belt figure comes from a classified listing [8] that the user's part matches.
- The 608 pitch-circle diameter differs between sources (14.700 mm [9] vs ~15.0 mm [10]);
  this alone moves 2 × BSF by 3.2 s (est.).
- Legacy-EQ6 period tables [36] apply to a different gear train; only the worm period carries
  over.
